hook.text: Cattle grazing under scattered trees gain more weight than cattle on open pasture. Shade reduces heat stress.

buildup.text: Silvopasture combines trees, forage grasses, and livestock on the same land. Each element benefits the others.

discovery.text: Trees provide shade and shelter. Cattle fertilize the soil. Grass protects tree roots from compaction.

twist.text: Project Drawdown ranks silvopasture as one of the top climate solutions—sequestering carbon in both trees and soil.

climax.text: In Colombia, silvopasture farms produce 4× more milk per hectare than treeless pastures.

punchline.text: Add trees to pasture. Happier cows. More milk. Stored carbon. Everyone wins.

quiz.question: Why do cattle perform better in silvopasture systems?
options: Tree shade reduces heat stress, improving weight gain and milk production

details.summary: Silvopasture combines trees, forage plants, and livestock grazing on the same land. It is one of the most effective land management practices for carbon sequestration, animal welfare, and farm profitability.
details.whyItMatters: Project Drawdown ranks silvopasture as one of the top solutions for reversing climate change in agriculture. It sequesters carbon above and below ground while improving animal welfare and pasture productivity.
takeaways: Silvopasture integrates trees with pasture grazing for multiple co-benefits
Livestock benefit from shade, shelter, and diverse forage under tree canopies
It ranks among the top climate solutions according to Project Drawdown

faq.question: How does silvopasture benefit livestock compared to open pasture?
faq.answer: Trees provide shade that reduces heat stress, which improves animal weight gain and milk production. Diverse tree forage supplements grass nutrition. Shelter from wind and rain reduces energy expenditure, and healthier animals need fewer veterinary interventions.

faq.question: Why is silvopasture considered such a powerful climate solution?
faq.answer: Silvopasture sequesters carbon in tree biomass and soil simultaneously, stores 5-10 times more carbon per hectare than open pasture, and reduces methane emissions from cattle by improving their diet with tree fodder and reducing heat stress.
